answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut on the constrained component, and the primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew. Memory c2 (verified) confirms a previous low-cost vendor switch cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, which directly supports hitting the 18% target. The assembly line runs at 94% with no buffer (14 days), so I will not switch vendors AND defer onboarding risk; I will run a structured pilot with a short dual-source ramp, keeping the incumbent under month-to-month terms until the new vendor's quality and on-time delivery are confirmed. Memory c4 supports renegotiation if margins can be recovered from the incumbent in parallel. Memory c6 suggests a multi-year lock with whoever wins, but only after the pilot validates the switch. In short: verify c2, then pilot a primary switch to the low-cost vendor with the incumbent on standby, leveraging c4-style negotiation to push price/tems during transition.
